  "verdict": "approve",
  "summary": "Read-only review of job J_UI (app.js, index.html, styles.css, all new files) against plan/contract.json, architecture.md, design.md, design.json and decisions.md. I read the whole diff.patch and traced every fetch call in candidate/app.js against the unchanged candidate/server.py to check status codes, response shapes and error bodies. I found no blocking defects. There are three advisories: a narrow race where a newly added todo can be missing from the view, a deliberate change from 'disabled' to aria-busy for the busy state, and gate logs that were missing from the review copy. I did not run anything. Gate results are taken from the review.json summaries only.",
  "evidence": {
    "requirements": "R4: index.html has visible labels for #new-list ('New list'), #rename-list ('New name for this list') and #new-todo ('New todo'). It has the #list-toggle picker with aria-expanded and aria-controls=list-panel, a #list-panel nav, three .filter buttons with aria-pressed (All/Active/Done), and #status with role=status and aria-live=polite. Assets load from local /styles.css and /app.js only, and both are in server.py STATIC. R5 (in code): switchList (app.js:431) switches the list, updates the toggle name and heading, and closes the phone menu with focus returned. Adding a todo, toggling a checkbox (PATCH done), the filters (GET ?status=), creating a list (POST), renaming (PATCH) and deleting with a confirm that names the list and its todo count (app.js:751) are all wired up. Inbox hides Rename/Delete (renderHeader, app.js:153) and the server also enforces this (lists_rename/lists_delete return 400). The empty state shows 'Nothing here yet'. R1-R3 belong to the server and are unchanged here.",
  "correctness": "Checked against the API contract: 204 returns null; errors come back as {error} through ApiFailure, and status 0 means a network failure. POST /api/todos sends {listId:int, title}, matching the server's int check. The GET todos query uses list and status, matching todos_index. A 404 on loading todos falls back to Inbox through loadLists and avoids a loop, because currentId=null makes changed=false. Stale responses are handled with a sequence number plus AbortController in loadTodos and listsSeq in loadLists. Double submits are blocked by state.busy flags, and pendingTodos blocks overlapping writes to one todo. A failed checkbox PATCH re-renders from the unchanged state, so the box reverts. A 404 on deleting a todo or list is treated as already deleted. Drafts are cleared only if the input is unchanged (app.js:496, 639). Escape order: the rename input calls preventDefault, and the document handler skips events where defaultPrevented is set (app.js:410), so the first Escape cancels rename and the second closes the menu. I found one narrow race, recorded as an advisory.",
  "scope": "The diff touches only app.js, index.html and styles.css. These match review.json paths and the J_UI job paths in contract.json. server.py does not appear in diff.patch, and candidate/server.py is the backend the UI was checked against. There are no new dependencies, build steps or external network origins.",
  "tests": "review.json records exit code 0 for G_API (lists, todos, validation, filters, cascade delete, restart persistence), G_UI (served HTML, labelled controls, picker, status region, assets) and G_BROWSER (journeys at phone and laptop widths). The log files in review.json (logs/G_*.log) are not in this review copy, so I could not check what the gates assert or that they ran against digest db380a44…. Failure-mode coverage that design.md requires, such as a network failure keeping the draft and the empty-title validation error, is implemented in code. I could not confirm that any gate exercised it.",
  "maintainability": "One IIFE with no dependencies, split into sections for transport, elements, state, rendering, loading, menu, filters, todos and lists. The server is the source of truth: after local updates, loadLists() refreshes counts. Local count changes (list.active/total) are guesses that the refresh overwrites, so they do not create a second source of truth. There are no retry loops and no hidden fallbacks: every failure path posts a message to #status.",
  "security": "All server-supplied text (list names, todo titles) is written with textContent or setAttribute, never innerHTML, so stored titles cannot inject script. The values used in querySelector selectors come from numeric ids the server returns. localStorage holds only a numeric list id, and restoreCurrent checks it against /^\\d+$/. No login on the home network is an accepted risk (decisions.md D3). This UI adds no new privileged operations, and Inbox protection is enforced on the server, not only hidden in the UI.",
  "design": "Follows direction B. Below 720px (max-width 719.98px) the panel is a fixed menu under the top bar, hidden unless data-open is set. At 720px and up there is a sticky sidebar and the toggle is hidden. The touch target is 44px (--target) on buttons, inputs and todo labels. Focus is visible through :focus-visible. Escape and tapping outside close the phone menu, and Escape returns focus to the toggle. Long titles and names wrap (overflow-wrap:anywhere), and the toggle name is truncated with an ellipsis, so a 320px width should not scroll sideways. I inferred this and did not measure it. Motion is limited to color transitions that only run under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. After adding a todo, focus stays on #new-todo. There is one change from design.json, recorded as an advisory: the Add button gets aria-busy while saving instead of being disabled."
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "advisory",
      "path": "app.js",
      "evidence": "app.js:497-500 adds the new todo to state.todos only when state.todosKey === todoKey(). Suppose the user adds a todo while a loadTodos request for the same list and filter is still in flight, for example right after switching lists. If the threaded server answers that GET before the POST insert commits, the GET's result becomes authoritative without the new todo. The follow-up loadLists() at app.js:510 refreshes only counts, not todos. The list count then shows +1 but the todo is not visible until the user changes filter or list. This is inferred, not reproduced, and needs sub-second timing.",
      "recommendation": "After a successful POST, if a todo load for the current key is still in flight (todosState === 'loading'), call loadTodos() again or merge the new todo once that load finishes. To check, delay GET /api/todos in a browser test and submit a todo while it is pending."

Duplicate submits are still blocked by state.busy.addTodo (app.js:476). The behavior is safe, but it is a documented change from the design handoff.",
      "recommendation": "Have the planner/designer confirm that aria-busy plus the submit guard is acceptable, or update design.json so the spec and the implementation agree."
    },
